title: Have you seen Bigfoot? Bancroft Canadian Tire and police hope so
excerpt: Store's sasquatch statues went missing last month, and police are now involved as staff suspect they were stolen.
content:
Bigfoot has been reported missing in Bancroft.

But this isn’t a case of a storied creature who wants to remain hidden in the Canadian wilderness.

It’s the case of two hulking sasquatch statues reported stolen from their places outside the town’s Canadian Tire store. They were discovered missing on Thursday, general manager Eliza Davis said.

Each statue stands about more than two metres tall. Davis said they were ordered from an outside vendor as part of an effort to make the store “more fun.”

She and other employees on Thursday were moving other items in front of the store after receiving a shipment of fall plants.

“I was putting one of the flowers where one of the yetis used to be, and I was like, ‘What used to be here?’” said Davis, who then remembered the statues.

Both the sasquatch and yeti are legendary tall, hairy bipeds.

“I was like, ‘Oh, good, we sold them. They’re going to good homes.’”

That’s when she checked the store’s inventory and saw they were still listed as being in stock.

Davis said she combed through the video recordings and found imagery of a man hauling away the statues in separate trips starting at 1:20 a.m. on Aug. 18.

“It was interesting to watch him pick it up,” she said. The hollow statues are “not that heavy” but would have required effort to move.

Davis said the man drove off fairly quickly with the first one.

“It’s a little funny,” she said of the video. “The yeti’s legs are sticking out the back.”

Davis laughed as she said the video showed the man stopping a short distance from the store, apparently to try to cram the legs into the truck, before departing. The scene’s lighting prevented the camera from capturing licence plate information, she said.

The truck, this time with a trailer in tow and no licence plates, reappeared on video four hours later.

Davis said she watched as the man pulled down the statue, “grabbed the sasquatch by the hips, and threw him into the back” of the vehicle. She called police, and on Friday Davis posted a missing-persons-style poster with images of a statue, the driver, and truck. The poster directs tips to Bancroft’s Ontario Provincial Police detachment.

Police investigating

“We are still investigating,” Sgt. Erin Cranton, an East Region OPP spokesperson, said late Friday afternoon.

She said the truck in question is described as a black Dodge Ram pickup towing a utility trailer. Davis said the truck appeared to have a rear cap.

As stolen property goes, the statues are “not something we would see every day,” yet it’s “still something that doesn’t belong to another person,” Cranton said.

“We’re looking for people to come forward if they know who’s responsible.

“I think seven-foot sasquatch statues would be pretty hard to miss if they’re out there somewhere.

“We’d like them returned.”

Editor’s Picks

Selfies with the sasquatch

Introduced to the store’s front parking lot in spring 2025, the sasquatch statues proved to be a popular attraction.

It stinks that they’re missing, Davis said, and not only because of their value: people loved seeing and being photographed with them.

She wondered why someone would steal them.

“What are you going to do with that? You’re … probably going to sell it or go take it out in the forest and shoot it or something. I don’t know.”

Lock up your dinosaurs

The first statue was sold last year to a retreat with “Bigfoot” in its name, Davis said.

Staff this year had ordered two more, but even at a lower price, they didn’t sell.

“We kind of just kept them around because they were kind of fun. It was so fun to see us tagged on social media with people with the yeti. It was so great.”

Store staff members have since taken precautions to protect their other large statues.

“We moved our moose … and we’ve bolted our bears down to the ground.”

She said she’s a little less concerned about the much larger Spinosaurus, a fearsome dinosaur. It’s more expensive, but much larger and would be harder to move. Still, she said, it’s heading into storage for rest of the season.

“We put that guy behind bars.”

Anyone with information about the case should call police at 1-888-310-1122 or make an anonymous tip to Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477). Crime Stoppers tips may be eligible for a cash reward.
